results.note: IMSLP: composed 1943–44, average 25 minutes (27 is within tolerance); 4 movements ending Allegretto (the Jewish-dance finale).

Year disagrees between sources: the publisher (Opus Imprints) gives 'Date written: 1987' (commissioned by the St. Paul Chamber Orchestra, premiered January 1987); Wikipedia's work list gives 1986 and says it was premiered as 'Divertimento' on 25 January 1987. 1986 is likely the completion year, so it is left unchanged. Publisher duration approx. 17 minutes confirms 17. The composer's note names early 20th-century American, Viennese, light classical, gypsy and Broadway styles and a Chassidic melody in movement 2; 'ragtime' is a fair gloss of the first. The publisher now spells the name Schoenfeld; the violin catalogue spells it Schoenfield.
IMSLP: dated 16 October 1785; also called Piano Quartet No. 1.
IMSLP: 1842; movements include Andante cantabile and Finale. Vivace.

IMSLP: c. 1876, 12–15 minutes; Wikipedia: one complete movement (Nicht zu schnell) plus a 24-bar scherzo sketch, begun when Mahler was 'around 15 or 16', first performed 10 July 1876, typically 10–15 minutes. Minutes 12 and form 'short' are borderline but acceptable; 'written at 16' could read 'at 15 or 16'.
IMSLP: 1861, 40 minutes, finale Rondo alla Zingarese.
IMSLP: composed 1876–79, first performed 14 February 1880, revised 1883 with a new finale (published 1884). '1883' alone dates only the revision.
IMSLP: 1819, 40 minutes, violin, viola, cello, double bass, piano; 4th movement variations on Die Forelle.
IMSLP: 1842, 30 minutes; 2nd movement In modo d'una marcia.
IMSLP: 1864, 41 minutes.
IMSLP: FWV 7, 1879; IMSLP average 40 minutes, recordings typically 35–38, so 36 stands.
IMSLP: 1887, 40 minutes (38 within tolerance); 2nd movement Dumka, 3rd Scherzo (Furiant). B. 155 exists but the violin catalogue does not use B. numbers for Dvořák.
IMSLP: 1907, 30 minutes.
IMSLP: 1940; five movements Prelude, Fugue, Scherzo, Intermezzo, Finale.
IMSLP: April–May 1824 (Mendelssohn was 15), 28–32 minutes, violin, 2 violas, cello, double bass, piano.
IMSLP: 1889–91, dedicated to Ysaÿe; matches the violin catalogue entry 1658.
IMSLP: 1777; Allegro, Adagio (B minor, pizzicato strings), Rondo.
IMSLP: 1781, written for Friedrich Ramm.
IMSLP: 1786; first edition Artaria 1788; instrumentation 'clarinet (or violin), viola, piano'.
IMSLP: 1789, written for Anton Stadler.

Added the names people actually use: 'Gassenhauer Trio' (Wikipedia) and 'Clarinet Trio' (Henle's 'Klarinettentrios'; IMSLP also lists 'Piano Trio No. 4'). Scoring 'clarinet (or violin), cello, piano' confirmed on IMSLP and Wikipedia; finale variations on 'Pria ch'io l'impegno' from Weigl's L'amor marinaro. Year: Wikipedia says composed 1797, published 1798; IMSLP says 1798. Weigl's opera opened 15 October 1797, so 1797–98; 1797 left unchanged.
IMSLP: 1799–1800 (completed early 1800, premiered 2 April 1800); six movements; '1799' is the usual composition year.
IMSLP: February–1 March 1824, 60 minutes; adds a second violin to Beethoven's Septet scoring.
IMSLP: 1849, average 30 minutes (33 within tolerance); premiered 1850 with Joachim on violin.
IMSLP: October 1853, 4 pieces, 'clarinet (or violin), viola, piano'.
IMSLP: 1865, 29 minutes; composed for natural horn with a cello option from the start, and a viola version of the horn part added in 1884 — both alternatives sanctioned by Brahms.

The first edition parts (Simrock, Berlin 1892, plate 9711, 6 parts) include a 'Solo Viola (alternative for clarinet)' part, Brahms's own arrangement (IMSLP version history: arranged for viola and string quartet by Brahms, 1891–92). IMSLP: 1891, 37 minutes.
IMSLP: 1895, 34 minutes (32 within tolerance), F-sharp minor (the Breitkopf parts wrongly say A major).
IMSLP: 1905, 12 minutes, harp, flute, clarinet, 2 violins, viola, cello.
IMSLP: 1919, clarinet, 2 violins, viola, cello, piano; written for the Zimro Ensemble.

The stage work is 1918 (premiered Lausanne, 28 September 1918); the suite for all seven players is a later version, first given as a concert suite in London in 1920 under Ansermet (Wikipedia), published by Chester 1922 — hence the house form '1918 (1920)'. Scoring confirmed (cornet, often played on trumpet). 25 minutes is typical for the suite (IMSLP's 35 is the complete stage music).
IMSLP: 1938, 17–20 minutes, dedicated to Goodman and Szigeti; finale violin scordatura G#-D-A-Eb.

Wikipedia: composed 1940–41, premiered 15 January 1941 at Stalag VIII-A, eight movements, about 50 minutes; movement VI played by all four in unison; movements V (cello) and VIII (violin) are the slow Louanges.

fixes.notes: Klezmer clarinettist, changing between several clarinets (bass clarinet included), with string quartet; played without a break

results.note: Boosey & Hawkes: 1994, 'for clarinet (or Klezmer clarinet) and string quartet', duration 33' (IRCAM's catalogue gives the same); 40 is too long. West Cork Music's concert listing says 37. 'On three clarinets' is not supported: West Cork Music's note lists B-flat, A, bass and C clarinets ('four different instruments'), and the Kronos/Krakauer recording is reported to use clarinet, bass clarinet and basset horn, so the count is left out. Played without a break (West Cork).

The 1681 print is titled 'Sonate a tre, doi violini e violone, o arciliuto, col basso per l'organo … Opera prima'; 'da chiesa' is a modern description, not the published name. 'Trio Sonatas, Op. 1' matches the violin catalogue's set names for Vivaldi Op. 1 and Handel Op. 5. Movements Grave–Allegro–Adagio–Allegro confirmed.

Added 'Canon in D', the name most people use (Wikipedia: 'also known as Canon in D, P 37'). IMSLP: 3 violins and continuo, 6–7 minutes. Year left blank on purpose: IMSLP says 'c. 1680', but Wikipedia says the date and circumstances are unknown (Schulze's suggestion of a 1694 wedding is disputed); fill it only if the house wants IMSLP's 'c. 1680'.
IMSLP: Op. 5 No. 4, published 1739; five movements incl. Passacaille. Matches violin catalogue entry 2495.
IMSLP: Op. 1 No. 12, published 1705. Matches violin catalogue entry 3093 (its single-quoted nickname differs from house style but must match the violin entry).

The sonata ('Sonata sopr'il Soggetto Reale a traversa, violino e continuo', Largo–Allegro–Andante–Allegro) was published in 1747 as part of the Musical Offering, so that is its set; the title already names it. Scoring, key and year confirmed. Fix is a field-convention judgment; skip it if the house keeps set for opus groupings only.

IMSLP: Quatuor VI of the Nouveaux quatuors en six suites (Hamburg 1738), also known as Paris Quartet No. 12 (added as aka); 6 movements ending Distrait – Modéré; scoring 'flute, violin, viola da gamba (or cello), continuo' as printed in 1738, so the cello alternative is sanctioned.

Title, numbering (No. 4, G. 448, 'Fandango'), 1798 and the four movements (Pastorale, Allegro maestoso, Grave assai, Fandango) are confirmed. Unverified: that the castanets are 'ad lib.' and sanctioned. Program notes say Boccherini added castanets in the Fandango, but the surviving source (François de Fossa's manuscript parts on IMSLP) and IMSLP's instrumentation list only guitar and string quartet; I found no source calling them ad libitum. 'optional: percussion' is plausible but unproven.

IMSLP: P. 101, 1914, voice and string quartet, Shelley in Roberto Ascoli's Italian translation (Ricordi 1918); the violin catalogue gives Respighi's P. numbers (Poema autunnale, P. 146), so the title should too. Mezzo-soprano confirmed by IMSLP's recording (Jennifer Johnson Cano).

Wise Music (G. Schirmer): 1931, medium voice and string quartet, 9 minutes (8 within tolerance); Op. 3 per Wikipedia's work list. Barber himself recorded it as a baritone; 'medium voice' is the published wording if the note is ever tightened.
IMSLP: 1907–08, soprano in movements 3 and 4 (Litanei, Entrückung, Stefan George).

composers.name: Mahler, Gustav
composers.note: 7 July 1860 – 18 May 1911. Wikipedia calls him Austro-Bohemian; 'Austrian' is the usual label (the violin catalogue uses 'Moravian-Austrian' for Ernst, so 'Bohemian-Austrian' would also be consistent).

composers.name: Golijov, Osvaldo
composers.note: Born 5 December 1960, La Plata. Wikipedia says 'Argentine composer'; he has worked in the US since the 1980s, so 'Argentine-American' fits the violin catalogue's style for émigrés (Austrian-American, Italian-American).

note: 45 works checked. Main fixes: Fauré Op. 15 year 1879 (rev. 1883); Brahms Clarinet Quintet gains the viola alternative printed in the 1892 first edition; Golijov 33 minutes (publisher) not 40, and 'three clarinets' removed; Stravinsky suite year 1918 (1920); Respighi title gets P. 101; Corelli set renamed to the house form 'Trio Sonatas, Op. 1'. Doubts: Schoenfield year (1986 vs 1987) and Boccherini's castanets 'ad lib.'.
